modules.name: Definition and Properties of Centre of Mass

blocks.title: Core Concept
blocks.text:
The Centre of Mass (COM) of a system is the point where the total mass of the system can be considered to be concentrated for translational motion analysis.

  • Properties of COM :-
1. For symmetrical bodies with uniform mass distribution, the centre of mass aligns with the centre of symmetry or geometric centre.

2. For a given shape, the centre of mass depends on mass distribution and is closer to denser regions.

3. The Centre of mass may not correspond to a physical mass and can lie inside or outside the body.

Centre of Mass of Discrete Mass System :-

$x_{\text{CM}} = \dfrac{\sum m_i x_i}{\sum m_i}$

$y_{\text{CM}} = \dfrac{\sum m_i y_i}{\sum m_i}$

$z_{\text{CM}} = \dfrac{\sum m_i z_i}{\sum m_i}$

Centre of Mass of Two Particle System :-

${\vec{r}}_{\text{CM}} = \frac{m_1 {\vec{r}}_1 + m_2 {\vec{r}}_2}{m_1 + m_2}$

COM of continuous mass distribution :-

  • Position of COM :-

$x_{cm} = \dfrac{\int x \, dm}{\int \, dm}, \quad y_{cm} = \dfrac{\int y \, dm}{\int \, dm}, \quad z_{cm} = \dfrac{\int z \, dm}{\int \, dm}$    ,$\mathbf{r}_{\text{cm}} = \dfrac{\int \mathbf{r} \, dm}{M}$
Types of Mass Densities

(a) Linear Mass Density (For 1-D Objects) :-

$\lambda = \dfrac{m}{L}$

(b) Areal Mass Density (For 2-D Objects) :-

$\sigma = \dfrac{m}{A}$

(c) Volumetric Mass Density (For 3-D Objects) :-

$\rho = \dfrac{m}{V}$

blocks.title: Example-2
blocks.question: The position vector of three particles of masses m1 = 1 kg, m2 = 2 kg and m3 = 3 kg are $\vec{\mathbf{r}}_1$=$(\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + \hat{k})m$ ,$\vec{\mathbf{r}}_2$=$(\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k})m$ and $\vec{\mathbf{r}}_3$=$(2\hat{i} - \hat{j} - \hat{k})m$ respectively. Find the position vector of their centre of mass?
blocks.answer:
Answer-

$\dfrac{1}{2} ( 3 \hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k} )$

$r_{\text{COM}} = \dfrac{m_1 r_1 + m_2 r_2 + m_3 r_3}{m_1 + m_2 + m_3}$

$r_{\text{COM}}$= $ \dfrac{     (1)(\hat{i} + 4 \hat{j} + \hat{k}) +      (2)(\hat{i} +  \hat{j} + \hat{k}) +      (3)(2 \hat{i} - \hat{j} -  \hat{k}) }{1 + 2 + 3}$

$r_{\text{COM}}$=$\dfrac{1}{2} ( 3 \hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k} )$

$r_{\text{COM}} = \dfrac{3\hat{\imath}}{2} +\dfrac{\hat{\jmath}}{2}$

modules.name: Calculation of Centre of Mass for Continuous Systems

blocks.title: Core Concept
blocks.text:
Uniform Symmetric Bodies :- For symmetrical bodies having homogeneous distribution of mass, COM Coincides with the centre of symmetry or the geometrical centre.

Centre of Mass of composite bodies :- Bodies which consist of two or more than two individual body (continuous).

$x_{\text{CM}} = \dfrac{m_d x_d + m_s x_s}{m_d + m_s}$

($m_s$ is mass of square,$m_d$ is mass of disc)

Centre of Mass of Truncated Bodies :-

If a portion of a body is taken out, the remaining portion may be considered as,

[Original mass (M) – mass of the removed part (m)] = {original mass (M)} + {– mass of the removed part (m)}

$x_{\text{CM}} = \dfrac{M x - m x'}{M - m}$

$y_{\text{CM}} = \dfrac{M y - m y'}{M - m}$

$z_{\text{CM}} = \dfrac{M z - m z'}{M - m}$

(x', y', z' represent the COM of the removed part)

Discrete Systems :-

  • $\vec{R}_{cm} = \dfrac{\sum_{i=1}^{n} m_i \vec{r}_i}{\sum_{i=1}^{n} m_i}$
Continuous Systems :-

  • $\vec{R}_{cm} = \dfrac{\int \vec{r} \, dm}{\int \, dm}$
  • $dm = \rho \, dV$
  • $dm = \sigma \, dA$
  • $dm = \lambda \, dx$
Velocity of COM :-

$\overrightarrow{\mathbf{V}}_{\mathrm{cm}}=\dfrac{d \overrightarrow{\mathbf{r}}_{\mathrm{cm}}}{d t}=\dfrac{m_1 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{v}}_1+m_2 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{v}}_2+m_3 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{v}}_3+\ldots}{m_1+m_2+m_3}$

Acceleration of COM :-

$\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}_{\mathrm{cm}}=\dfrac{d \overrightarrow{\mathbf{v}}_{\mathrm{cm}}}{d t}=\dfrac{m_1 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}_1+m_2 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}_2+m_3 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}_3+\ldots}{m_1+m_2+m_3}$

blocks.title: Example -1
blocks.question: Find position of COM.
blocks.answer:
Answer: $(\frac{L}{4},\frac{L}{4})$

Centre of mass of rods are

$\left( \frac{L}{2}, 0 \right), \left( 0, \frac{L}{2} \right)$

$x_{\text{CM}} = \dfrac{m \left( \frac{L}{2} \right) + m(0)}{2m}$=$\frac{L}{4}$

$y_{\text{CM}} = \dfrac{m(0) + m\left(\frac{L}{2}\right)}{2m}$=$\frac{L}{4}$

So, position of COM  $(\frac{L}{4},\frac{L}{4})$

blocks.title: Example-2
blocks.question: Find the centre of mass of a uniform disc of radius 'a' from which a circular section of radius 'b' has been removed. The centre of the hole is at a distance c from the centre of the disc.
blocks.answer:
$M = \sigma \pi a^2$

$m = \sigma \pi b^2$

$x_{\text{CM}} = \dfrac{ (\sigma \pi a^2) \cdot 0 - (\sigma \pi b^2) \cdot c }{ \sigma \pi a^2 - \sigma \pi b^2 }$=$-\frac{b^2 c}{a^2 - b^2}$

So, coordinate of COM of remaining portion is  $(\dfrac{b^2 c}{a^2 - b^2}, 0)$

modules.name: Conservation of Linear Momentum and Applications

blocks.title: Core Concepts
blocks.text:
Linear Momentum :- It is equal to the product of mass of the system with velocity of its COM, $\vec{p}_{\text{cm}} = M \vec{V}_{\text{cm}}$

Conservation of Linear Momentum and Impulse :- Total linear momentum of a system of particles remains conserved in a time interval in which impulse of external forces is zero. $\overrightarrow{F_{\text{ext}}} = \overrightarrow{0} \Rightarrow \overrightarrow{a_{\text{cm}}}= \overrightarrow{0}$ then  $\overrightarrow{p_{\text{system}}} = \overrightarrow{0}$.

Effect of External Force on Centre of Mass :-

$\overrightarrow{F_{\text{ext}}} = \overrightarrow{0} \quad \Rightarrow \quad \overrightarrow{a_{\text{CM}}} = \overrightarrow{0}$

• Principle of conservation of linear momentum
$\vec{p}_{\text{initial}} = \vec{p}_{\text{final}}$• Application of Conservation of Linear Momentum

1. When bullet remains embedded in the block :-

Velocity of system-$V = \dfrac{m v}{M + m}$

Maximum height gained by block $h = \dfrac{V^2}{2g}$=$\dfrac{m^2 v^2}{2g (M + m)^2}$

2. If bullet emerges out of the block :

$V_2 = \dfrac{m \left( v - v_1 \right)}{ M}$

Effect of External Force on COM :

• Conservation of linear momentum states that the total momentum of a closed system remains constant if no external forces act on it.
Firing a Bullet From a Gun :-

$m\overrightarrow{v} + M\overrightarrow{V} = \overrightarrow{0}$

$\overrightarrow{V} = -\dfrac{m}{M} \overrightarrow{v}$

blocks.title: Example - 1
blocks.question: Two persons A & B are standing on a plank as shown in figure. If A & B exchange their position find displacement of the plank.
blocks.answer:
As there is no external force acting on the system so COM of system does not change its position. Let plank moves 'x' distance.

$40( 10 +  x ) + 100(x) + 60 ( x - 10 ) = 0$

$400 + 40x + 100x + 60x -600 = 0$

$-200 + 200x = 0$

$x = 1m$
blocks.prompt: Two persons A & B are standing on a plank as shown in figure. If A & B exchange their position find displacement of the plank.

blocks.title: Example-2
blocks.question: A sphere of mass m is rolling down on a wedge of mass M. When sphere reaches at lowest point then find distance moved by wedge in horizontal direction.
blocks.answer:
Answer

$x = \dfrac{mR}{M + m}$

Let distance moved by wedge is $'x'$

$m(R-x)-Mx=0$

$mR-mx-Mx=0$

$mR-x(M+m) = 0$

$x = \dfrac{mR}{M + m}$
blocks.prompt: A sphere of mass m is rolling down on a wedge of mass M. When sphere reaches at lowest point then find distance moved by wedge in horizontal direction.

blocks.title: Example-3
blocks.question: Find maximum compression in the spring.
blocks.answer:
Answer $x = \sqrt{\dfrac{1080}{k}}$

Note : At the state of max. compression or max. elongation, velocity of connecting blocks must be same .Apply COLM

$3\times30=3v+2v$

$v=18m/s$

$\dfrac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 30^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 2 \times 18^2 + \dfrac{1}{2} \times 18^2 + \dfrac{1}{2} k x^2$

$2700 = 18^2 \times 5 + k x^2$

$1080 = k x^2$

$x = \sqrt{\dfrac{1080}{k}}$

blocks.title: Core Concepts
blocks.text:
Collision :- Collision is the brief interaction between two bodies during which they exert large forces on each other.

Direct Collision :- When a rubber ball hits the floor, it briefly contacts the surface and changes velocity, demonstrating a collision with physical contact.

Indirect Collision :- In Rutherford's experiment, when an alpha particle passes near a gold nucleus, it is deflected in a short time, indicating a change in direction without physical contact.

Types of Collision

1. Head-on Collision :- A head-on collision occurs when particles move along the same straight line before and after the collision.

2. Oblique Collision :- An oblique collision occurs when particles move in the same plane at different angles before and after the collision.

Coefficient of Restitution :-

$e = \dfrac{\text{Velocity of separation along the line of impact}}{\text{Velocity of approach along the line of impact}}$=$\dfrac{|v_B - v_A|}{|u_A - u_B|}$

e=0 For perfectly inelastic

$0<\mathrm{e}<1 \text { For inelastic collision }$:

e=1 perfectly elastic

blocks.title: Example-1
blocks.question: A ball of mass 2 kg moving with a speed of 5 m/s collides directly with another ball of mass 3 kg moving in the same direction with a speed of 4 m/s. The coefficient of restitution is 2/3. Find the velocities after collision.
blocks.answer:
Ans.  $\mathrm{v}_1=4 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \text { and } \mathrm{v}_2=4.67 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$

Denoting the first ball by A and the second ball by B, velocities immediately before and after the impact are shown in the figure.

$\text { By COLM : } 2(5)+3(4)=2 \mathrm{v}_1+3 \mathrm{v}_2 \Rightarrow 2 \mathrm{v}_1+3 \mathrm{v}_2=22$

$\text { By definition of e : } e=\dfrac{v_2-v_1}{u_1-u_2} \Rightarrow \dfrac{2}{3}=\dfrac{v_2-v_1}{5-4} \Rightarrow 3 v_2-3 v_1=2$

$\mathrm{v}_1=4 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \text { and } \mathrm{v}_2=4.67 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$

blocks.question: A body of 2 kg mass having velocity 3 m/s collides with a body of 1 kg mass moving with a velocity of 4m/s in the opposite direction. After collision both bodies stick together and move with a common velocity. Find the velocity in m/s.

blocks.title: Common Mistakes
blocks.text:
• Ignoring Conservation Laws: Incorrect application, especially in inelastic collisions.
  • Misapplying Coefficient of Restitution: Confusing $e$'s application across collision types.
  • Unit Errors: Inconsistent unit conversion leading to calculation errors.

blocks.title: Core Concepts
blocks.text:
Head on Elastic Collision :-

$\overrightarrow{v_1}= \dfrac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2} \overrightarrow{u_1} + \dfrac{2m_2 \overrightarrow{u_2}}{m_1 + m_2}$

$\overrightarrow{v_2} = \dfrac{m_2 - m_1}{m_1 + m_2} \overrightarrow{u_2} + \dfrac{2m_1 \overrightarrow{u_1}}{m_1 + m_2}$

Head on Inelastic Collision :-

$\overrightarrow{v_1}=\dfrac{m_1-e m_2}{m_1+m_2} \overrightarrow{v_1}+\dfrac{(1+e) m_2 \vec{v}_2}{m_1+m_2}$

$\vec{v}_2=\dfrac{m_2-e m_1}{m_1+m_2} \vec{u}_2+\dfrac{(1+e) m_1 \vec{u}_1}{m_1+m_2}$

Loss in K.E. = $\dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{m_1 m_2}{m_1 + m_2} (1 - e^2) (\overrightarrow{u}_1 - \overrightarrow{u}_2)^2$

Head on perfectly inelastic collision :-

$\mathbf{v} = \dfrac{m_1 u_1 + m_2 u_2}{m_1 + m_2}$

Loss in K.E =$\dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{m_1 m_2}{m_1 + m_2} (u_1 - u_2)^2$

Bouncing of Ball :-

Velocity after the nth rebound :- $v_n=e^n \sqrt{2 g h}$

Height attained by the ball after nth rebound :- $h_n = e^{2n} h$

Time taken in nth rebound :- $t_n = e^n t$

Total time taken in bouncing before the ball stops

$T = \sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}} \left( \frac{1+e}{1-e} \right)$

Distance Covered by The Ball Before It Stops:- $h \left( \dfrac{1 + e^2}{1 - e^2} \right)$

blocks.title: Core Concepts
blocks.text:
Oblique Collision :- A collision in which the particles move in the same plane at different angles before and after the collision is called Oblique Collision.

By COLM along x-axis :-  $m_1 u_1 + m_2 u_2 = m_1 v_1 \cos \theta + m_2 v_2 \cos \phi$

By COLM along y -axis :-  $0 + 0 = m_1 v_1 \sin \theta - m_2 v_2 \sin \phi$

By Conservation of Kinetic Energy,

$\dfrac{1}{2} m_1 u_1^2+\dfrac{1}{2} m_2 u_2^2=\dfrac{1}{2} m_1 v_1^2+\dfrac{1}{2} m_2 v_2^2$

blocks.title: Example-1
blocks.question: After perfectly inelastic collision between two identical balls moving with same speed in different directions ,the speed of the combined mass becomes half the initial speed. Find the angle between the two before collision.
blocks.answer:
Answer $\theta = 120^\circ$

Let $\theta$ be the desired angle and linear momentum is conserved.

$2 m v \cos \frac{\theta}{2}=2 m \frac{v}{2}$

$\cos \frac{\theta}{2}=\frac{1}{2}$

$\frac{\theta}{2}=60^{\circ}$

$\theta = 120^\circ$
blocks.prompt: After perfectly inelastic collision between two identical balls moving with same speed in different directions ,the speed of the combined mass becomes half the initial speed. Find the angle between the two before collision.

blocks.title: Example-2
blocks.question: The coefficient of restitution between a snooker ball and the side cushion is $\frac{1}{3}$.If the ball hits the cushion and then rebounds at right angles to its original direction ,show that the angle made with the side cushion by the direction of motion before and after impact are $60^\circ \quad \text{and} \quad 30^\circ$ respectively.
blocks.answer:
Answer The direction of motion before and after impact are at $60^\circ \quad \text{and} \quad 30^\circ$ to the cushion.

Let the original speed be $u$ in a direction making an angle $\theta$ with the side cushion .Using the law of restitution.

Relative speed of separation along common normal reaction =$e$(relative speed of approach)

$v = \dfrac{1}{3} (u \sin \theta)$

$\dfrac{u}{v} = \dfrac{3}{\sin \theta}$

$\tan \theta = \dfrac{u \cos \theta}{v} = \dfrac{3 \cos \theta}{\sin \theta}$

$\tan^2 \theta = 3$

$\tan \theta = \sqrt{3}$

$\theta = 60^\circ$

The direction of motion before and after impact are at $60^\circ \quad \text{and} \quad 30^\circ$ to the cushion.

$T = \sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}} \left( \frac{1+e}{1-e} \right)$

Distance Covered by The Ball Before It Stops:- $h \left( \dfrac{1 + e^2}{1 - e^2} \right)$

blocks.title: Core Concepts
blocks.text:
Oblique Collision :- A collision in which the particles move in the same plane at different angles before and after the collision is called Oblique Collision.

By COLM along x-axis :-  $m_1 u_1 + m_2 u_2 = m_1 v_1 \cos \theta + m_2 v_2 \cos \phi$

By COLM along y -axis :-  $0 + 0 = m_1 v_1 \sin \theta - m_2 v_2 \sin \phi$

By Conservation of Kinetic Energy,

$\dfrac{1}{2} m_1 u_1^2+\dfrac{1}{2} m_2 u_2^2=\dfrac{1}{2} m_1 v_1^2+\dfrac{1}{2} m_2 v_2^2$
